note: Every construct that earns must in the attributed graphs of the final measurement, read against the application's source by the assistant the declaration at the front of the thesis describes: the template or method around it for a condition, the route configuration for the address the construct resolves to and for every guard, resolver and canDeactivate that runs on the navigation. graph-census.mjs refuses to report a must construct that is not listed here.

sites.reading: Logo link routerLink="/" in the footer, which app.component.html renders unconditionally beside the outlet on every screen; '/' declares no guard or resolver and no screen it is drawn from declares canDeactivate. Drawn from every screen but '/', where it is a self-loop.
Logo link routerLink="/" at the top of the header, before the @if (authState$ | async) block, so outside every template condition; same reasoning as the footer logo.
Global Feed link to '/' outside the template conditions of the home template; drawn from /tag/:tag, which renders the home component, and a self-loop at '/'.

goToCreateState() calls this.router_.navigate(['create'], {queryParamsHandling: 'preserve'}) as its only statement; with no relativeTo the command resolves against the root, so '/create'. It is bound bare as (click)="goToCreateState()" on a toolbar button outside every template condition. Entering /create runs no guard (its route declares canDeactivate only, which runs on leaving it).

Toolbar logo [routerLink]="getWorkloadsStateName()", a method that returns the constant '/workloads'; the toolbar sits outside the *ngIf banner. The chrome component is the route component of the '' route whose children are every screen drawn; that level carries AuthGuard, which a navigation between two of its children does not run again. /search (SearchGuard) and /create (CanDeactivateGuard) declare canDeactivate and are held at may as sources, as the graph records.

Cancel button [routerLink]="'/sm-landing'" (type=button) outside every template condition. Source and target are children of the same '' route with UserLayoutComponent, whose deepLinkGuard and authGuard a navigation between its children does not run again; neither child declares a guard or resolver.

Cancel or Back button [routerLink] with '../' or '../../' outside every template condition. Angular resolves it against the segments the component's route consumed, so '../' drops one segment and '../../' two, which lands on the address recorded; the target screen declares no guard or resolver, and source and target sit in the same lazily loaded module under the same withShell level, whose AuthenticationGuard does not run again.
